clue.text: Precisely locate leg fielder's position

parts.note: pin is slang for a leg, as in 'unsteady on my pins'
point is a cricket fielding position square of the batsman on the off side

explanation.surface: A cricket captain sets a fielder exactly on the leg side.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, the leg side and point are both field areas, so the surface reads as one fielding instruction; 'leg' is really slang for a limb.
explanation.definitionFit: To pinpoint something is to identify its location with great accuracy, a direct verb synonym.

clue.text: Begin my laconic report on restaurant?

parts.note: a terse diner's report on a restaurant, '...', run together into one word

explanation.surface: Someone is told to start writing a short review of a restaurant they visited.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the pun: the shortest possible report of a meal at a restaurant is 'In it, I ate', which runs together into one eight-letter verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To initiate something is to start it off or set it going, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Badly cut, it's poor kind of meat

indicators.note: badly signals that the words cut, it's and poor are to be jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A butcher's clumsy slicing has ruined a cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges CUT, ITS and POOR together.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosciutto is Italian dry-cured ham, so it is one kind of meat.

clue.text: Error in a Conservative junior minister's position

parts.note: taken as written
a curacy is the post of a curate, a junior minister of the Church

explanation.surface: A Tory junior government minister has made a blunder in their role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junior minister' suggests government, but here it is a curate in the Church, whose post is a curacy.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaccuracy is a mistake or factual slip, so it is a synonym for error.

clue.text: Publication that's a bit old, needing revision

indicators.note: something needing revision must be reworked, so these letters are put into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A periodical is somewhat out of date and needs updating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needing revision' rearranges the letters of A BIT OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a popular newspaper, which is a kind of publication.

clue.text: Blunder in speech in House

indicators.note: in speech says the word for a blunder is heard rather than written

parts.note: a gaffe is a social blunder

explanation.surface: Someone makes a slip of the tongue during a speech in the House of Commons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in speech' says GAFFE (blunder) is only heard; written GAFF it is slang for one's home.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaff is British slang for a person's home or flat, as in 'come back to my gaff'.

clue.text: Doesn't rum get you this?

indicators.note: rum as an adjective means odd or strange, so the letters of the word before it are put in an odd order

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about whether rum leaves you intoxicated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' looks like the drink but is the anagram signal (rum = odd): DOESNT rearranged gives the answer, and the whole clue also defines it, since drinking rum gets you drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoned is slang for very drunk or intoxicated, which is what heavy rum drinking leaves you.

clue.text: Reticent about fighting, having turned tail, finally?

definitions.meaning: in the manner of one who runs away: the adverb-style ending 'finally' hints at a word built from a noun for a deserter plus -ly

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: someone who ends up turning tail behaves like a deserter, and the question mark admits the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone lacking courage avoids combat, so a fearful, faint-hearted person is reluctant to fight.

clue.text: Drink that's a degree 'igher in temperature returned

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

indicators.note: returned says the dropped-aitch word for hotter is read backwards

parts.note: higher in temperature is hotter; with the H dropped, as in 'igher, it becomes 'otter

explanation.surface: A drink advertised as a degree higher in temperature has been sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'igher shows a dropped aitch, so the word for higher in temperature loses its H too; 'returned' reads that shortened word backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaretto is an Italian almond-flavoured liqueur, so it is a drink.

clue.text: One growing sensitive wants Maoism reformed

indicators.note: reformed means formed again, so the letters of Maoism are put in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A Chinese political thinker grows touchy and wants the ideology changed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One growing sensitive' sounds like a person becoming touchy; it is a plant, the sensitive plant, whose leaves fold when touched.
explanation.definitionFit: The mimosa includes the sensitive plant, whose leaves curl up at a touch, so it is a growing thing that is sensitive.

clue.text: Lion intermittently seen in Africa, perhaps, in this state

indicators.note: perhaps signals that Africa is only a possible arrangement of these letters, with the letters of lion scattered intermittently among them

explanation.surface: A lion is spotted now and then on safari, somewhere far from this US state.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of LION appear intermittently among a rearrangement of AFRICA; 'perhaps' marks Africa as one possible order of its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: California is a state of the USA on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Formalities for this country in a certain decade

indicators.note: in says the country sits inside the long word, between the two parts named

parts.note: taken as written
decades such as the twenties, sixties or nineties all end in -ties

explanation.surface: Red tape a country faced during one particular decade.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Formalities' as FOR + the country + TIES, the ending shared by decades like the sixties: take FOR and TIES away and the African state is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Mali is a landlocked West African nation, the country this clue points to.

clue.text: Loveless marriage annulled after short time, not as planned

indicators.note: after places the word for annulled following the short time
love is zero, the letter O in tennis scoring, so loveless means without an O

parts.note: a union is a marriage
T is the abbreviation for time
an annulled marriage is ended

explanation.surface: A marriage without love was dissolved after only a short while.
explanation.walkthrough: Love = O (the tennis score of nil), so 'Loveless' takes O out of UNION.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unintended happens without being meant or planned, so it was not as planned.

clue.text: Breed dog who doesn't need lead now?

parts.note: a breed is a type or kind
a setter is a gun dog breed

explanation.surface: A breed of dog that is so obedient it no longer needs a leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' sounds like a dog's leash; it is the metal of type, which compositors once set by hand and which computer typesetting has made unnecessary.
explanation.definitionFit: A compositor once arranged metal type, but modern digital setting uses no metal at all, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Secure one kind of European cosmetic

parts.note: to nail is to fasten or secure
Polish describes a person from Poland, one kind of European

explanation.surface: A European woman fixes her make-up in place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' here is the nationality, though the answer reads it as a coating.
explanation.definitionFit: Varnish painted on fingernails is a cosmetic product used for beauty.

clue.text: Important, like position one takes in committee

definitions.text: like position one takes in committee
definitions.meaning: the letter I, standing for one, is the middle letter of the nine-letter word committee

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads 'one' as the letter I: in the word COMMITTEE, I is the fifth of nine letters, right in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something central is at the heart of things, so it is key or important.

clue.text: Cold skate, say, served on flat plate as seafood

indicators.note: served on, in a down clue, places the earlier pieces on top of the next

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a skate is a kind of ray, a flat fish
a fish is a flat plate of wood or iron used to strengthen a joint, as in a railway fishplate

explanation.surface: Chilled skate is presented on a flat dish as a fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat plate' looks like crockery but is a fish, the flat iron strip that joins rails or beams.
explanation.definitionFit: Crayfish are freshwater crustaceans eaten as shellfish, so they count as seafood.

clue.text: Elastic band concealed by notice

indicators.note: concealed by says the word for band sits inside the word for notice

parts.note: to spy something is to notice it
a ring is a circular band

explanation.surface: A rubber band was hidden behind a posted notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'notice' looks like a noun (a sign), but it is the verb, to spy.
explanation.definitionFit: Something springy bounces back into shape, so it is elastic or resilient.

clue.text: Pill taken by driver on his rounds

definitions.text: Pill taken by driver on his rounds

parts.words: Pill taken by driver on his rounds
parts.note: pill is slang for a ball; a driver is a long golf club, and rounds are rounds of golf, not a delivery driver's rounds

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a van driver taking medication on a delivery round; the driver is a club and the pill something it hits.
explanation.definitionFit: Pill is old slang for a ball, and a driver strikes one throughout a round on the course.

clue.text: Musical pieces, perhaps, supported by another town in Midlands

indicators.note: supported by, in a down clue, puts the next piece beneath

parts.note: musical pieces are works, as in a composer's works
op, short for opus, is another word for a musical work

explanation.surface: Music performed with backing from another town in the English Midlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another musical piece, an opus, abbreviated OP. Worksop is a market town in Nottinghamshire, in England's East Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: Worksop is a market town in north Nottinghamshire, part of the East Midlands region of England.

clue.text: Like War and Peace — unsigned, without Tolstoy's initial

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside places the word for unsigned around the letter

parts.note: an unsigned piece of writing is anonymous

indicators.note: initial takes the first letter of the name Tolstoy

explanation.surface: Tolstoy's War and Peace published without his name or initials on it.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes you think of the novel; the definition is the words 'war' and 'peace', which are opposites. 'without' is the old sense, outside.
explanation.definitionFit: War and peace are opposites, so the pair is antonymous, made of words of opposite meaning.

clue.text: The Origin of Species is presented as theory

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: origin of takes the first letter, where the word begins

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Darwin's book The Origin of Species is put forward as a scientific theory.
explanation.walkthrough: The title reads as one unit, but 'Origin of' takes the first letter of Species.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition or theory put forward to be argued, a close synonym.

clue.text: Subject to bombardment, hide

definitions.meaning: to bombard with missiles, as with stones or rain

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the verb to bombard with missiles; the other is the noun for an animal's skin.

clue.text: A book found in brisk second-hand trading area

indicators.note: found in says the pieces sit inside the word for brisk

parts.note: fleet means swift or brisk
Mark is a book of the New Testament

explanation.surface: A book picked up at a bustling second-hand market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brisk' sounds like the market's trade, but it gives FLEET, which holds A and MARK, the Gospel book.
explanation.definitionFit: A flea market is an open-air market selling used goods, so it is a second-hand trading place.

clue.text: It's a north-facing area for wine

indicators.note: in a down clue, facing north means reading upwards, so the letters go in reverse

explanation.surface: A south-facing slope is best for vines, but this vineyard faces north.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry, 'north-facing' means read upwards: ITS A becomes the Piedmont wine town.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a town and district in Piedmont, Italy, famous for its sparkling wine.

clue.text: Like some groups of people getting OK grade in test

indicators.note: in places the grade inside the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test
B is a decent but not top mark in a grading scale

explanation.surface: Some groups of students achieve a passable mark in an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'OK grade' is B, a merely satisfactory exam grade.
explanation.definitionFit: Tribal describes groups organised as tribes, so it applies to some groups of people.

clue.text: Possible cause of stabbing pains in the heel

definitions.text: Possible cause of stabbing pains in the heel

parts.words: Possible cause of stabbing pains in the heel
parts.note: a slim dagger causes stabbing pains, and a tall spiky shoe heel can cause pain in the foot

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a medical complaint; it describes a slim dagger and a high, thin shoe heel at once.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is both a thin dagger for stabbing and a tall thin heel on a woman's shoe.

clue.text: Runs into cave from which sea can be seen

definitions.text: from which sea can be seen

indicators.note: into says the abbreviation for runs goes inside the word for cave

parts.note: a pothole is a deep cave or shaft in limestone
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone runs into a sea cave with a view of the waves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cave' gives POTHOLE, a deep limestone cave, not a sea cave.
explanation.definitionFit: A porthole is a round window in a ship's side through which the sea can be seen.
